Toyota's origins can be traced to 1933, when an Automobile Division was established within Toyoda Automatic Loom Works devoted to the production of cars [d2], with the formal Automobile Division launch on September 1, 1933 [d3]. Toyota's first production car, the Model AA sedan, was released in 1936 [d6], and the company was formally incorporated as Toyota Motor Company, Ltd. on August 28, 1937, under the leadership of founder Kiichiro Toyoda [d3][d6][d8][d9]. Toyota's presence in the United States began in 1957, when two Toyopet Crown sedans arrived and Toyota Motor Sales, U.S.A., Inc. was established as a California corporation on October 31, 1957 [d5][d7]. The Toyota Corona, designed specifically for American drivers, went on sale in 1965 and became the first truly popular Toyota in America [d1][d8][d9].
